title: What If You Were Trapped in a ZOMBIE Outbreak?
description:
Glint has twenty minutes to get Nan onto the last boat out of a city full of the infected, and Nan can't run. Thirty days earlier, a strange fever hit the hospital: people who wander, stare at lights, walk towards noise and won't go near water. Glint can't fight it. So he does the only thing that works in a real epidemic: he learns how it spreads. Incubation, R nought, the SIR model, quarantine and why crowds are the danger, plus the real parasites that inspired it all (the zombie-ant fungus, Toxoplasma and rabies) and the Cornell University zombie outbreak model.

If an outbreak hit your city tomorrow, would you stay home, head for the hills, or follow the ice cream van? Tell me in the comments 👇

SOURCES
• Hughes et al., BMC Ecology 11:13 (2011); Andersen et al., American Naturalist 174 (2009): Ophiocordyceps unilateralis makes carpenter ants climb and bite a leaf before the fungus grows out
• Berdoy, Webster & Macdonald, Proc. R. Soc. B 267 (2000): Toxoplasma-infected rats lose their fear of cat odour
• WHO, Rabies fact sheet; CDC, Rabies: spread through saliva, usually a bite; hydrophobia (painful throat spasms)
• CDC, How flu spreads: people can spread flu about a day before symptoms
• Guerra et al., Lancet Infectious Diseases 17 (2017); Biggerstaff et al., BMC Infectious Diseases 14:480 (2014): R0 of measles (classically 12-18) and seasonal flu (median about 1.3)
• Kermack & McKendrick, Proc. R. Soc. A 115 (1927): the SIR epidemic model
• Alemi, Bierbaum, Myers & Sethna, "You Can Run, You Can Hide: The Epidemiology and Statistical Mechanics of Zombies", Physical Review E 92 (2015), arXiv:1503.01104 (Cornell; APS March Meeting 2015)
• Story is fiction: the Drift, its three-day hiding period, R of three, its fear of water and its treatment are made up; the science rules behind them are real.
